concepts.definition: F1, frames and context, concerns finite actors declaring, sizing, binding, activating, relating, auditing and revising bounded reference frames. Its instance premises are: the workspace exceeds one actor's competence, context, tools and access; evaluations are declared questions about a governed outcome; multiple frames and actors may overlap; workspace topology and capabilities change between activations; and actors may read owning sources or copied, projected or compressed surfaces. These are domain conditions, not commitments derived from finitude alone. P0 includes actor change without transfer of private memory and an open world. The table distinguishes recovered P0, independent P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6, and derived P4b/P5, including their stated extra premises; it attributes consequences and policy choices without owning the cited rules.

grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work this family governs, not
commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

concepts.label: Frames and context family

concepts.definition: A reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required by one evaluation family. It specifies a relation rather than a required schema or runtime carrier. Its declared tuple is attributed to FOUNDATIONS as ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩. An activated frame is one bounded engagement unit; selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision remain distinct functions.

grounding.quote: a reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations one evaluation family requires.

concepts.label: Reference frame

concepts.definition: The declared family of questions or predicates a frame supports, against which its sufficiency is testable. Inclusion concerns the question actually decided at the declared coordinates.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

concepts.label: Evaluation family

concepts.definition: The selected actor's declared capability boundary. Frame fit and adequate attention during actual use are distinct questions; context-size measurement addresses the former, while EVALUATION §7 supplies the actual-use evidence regime for the latter.

grounding.quote:
Whether the actor attends adequately to a frame that fits is a separate
question, answered by actual-use evidence under
[EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification); a size measurement
does not answer it

concepts.label: Capability envelope and actual-use adequacy

concepts.definition: Distinct frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authorities; actor identity is separate. Frame-set authority is human authority. Semantic law defines meaning, evidence supplies observations, evaluation applies the declared relation, the existing operation owner supplies any exact operation grant, and decision authority disposes the result. Coincidence in a lawful case does not collapse the kinds; a proxy's identity remains distinct from human authority.

grounding.quote: semantic law defines what the evaluation means, evidence supplies observations, the evaluator applies the declared relation, the existing operation owner supplies any operation grant, and decision authority disposes the result

concepts.label: Frame authority kinds and roles

concepts.definition: One result returned by a performed evaluation in its declared algebra: the FOUNDATIONS §4 core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, or an authorized refinement mapped into them. RF-012 applies, but does not define, their meanings. A nonperformed evaluation has no evaluation result; its stop state belongs to ACTIVATION §3.

grounding.quote:
that an evaluation not performed has no result,
its stop state being
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition).

concepts.label: Closed evaluation result

concepts.definition: A human-declared project selection of frames for a governed workspace and outcome, informed by practice, known failures, expertise, outcome risk and available actors. It need not be reconstructed bottom up or form a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated
development practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the governed
outcome's risk and knowledge of the available agents and other actors. The
declaration need not reconstruct the set from the workspace bottom up

concepts.label: Project frame set

concepts.definition: Seven distinct relational signatures, not callable-interface requirements: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) → frame_set; activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) → activated_frame or activation_refusal; evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) → result + evidence + residuals; conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) → decision, conflict or indeterminate; translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) → translated_value, declared_loss or refusal; audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) → coverage_ledger; revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) → proposed_frame_set_delta. Additional direct core outcomes are specified in the accompanying prose. Declaration belongs to §4, activation/evaluation to ACTIVATION §§1–2, result return/reuse to ACTIVATION §7, conjunction/translation to §6, coverage to §8, revision to §10; EVALUATION §7 qualifies each.

grounding.quote:
The frame and the functions over it remain distinct. An application may
realise the following relations in any conforming form; the signatures
describe relations, not callable software interfaces

concepts.label: Method functions

concepts.definition: Separate activations of several frames evaluating the same subject and returning closed results. Subject, manifold and evidence may overlap. This serves assurance independence, different evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives, without alone establishing all assurance-independence conditions.

grounding.quote:
Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations
and return closed results.

concepts.label: Independently activated co-evaluation

concepts.definition: A declared decision rule consumes several frames' closed results. Its required declaration and computation belong to FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results over the core algebra; this member defines no separate conjunction.

grounding.quote:
A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.
The rule, what it must state, and the conjunction it computes are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
over the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results);
this member defines no conjunction of its own.

concepts.label: Result conjunction

concepts.definition: A source frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside a target frame through a declared translation. Its declaration specifies source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.

grounding.quote:
One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The
translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions

concepts.label: Evidence or coordinate translation

concepts.definition: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation, declared by the owning application.

grounding.quote:
Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
relation. The owning application declares the composition

concepts.label: Material composition

concepts.definition: Ten optional frame relation kinds: disjoint means no shared material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for the declared evaluations; overlapping shares material variables, evidence or entities; complementary evaluations jointly inform one decision; alternative frames evaluate the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions; refinement resolves a distinction another frame aggregates; restriction evaluates a lawful subset of another domain; translated moves values/evidence through a declared coordinate map; temporal succession evaluates a changed basis later; composed joins frame relations into one governed evaluation/action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where a real authority or decomposition relation exists.

grounding.quote:
- governing and subordinate: one frame inherits declared constraints from
  another where a real authority or decomposition relation exists.

concepts.label: Frame relation kinds

concepts.definition: The workspace-coverage topic developed by the following coverage basis, inventory, lenses, ledger and coverage conditions.

grounding.quote: ## 8. Workspace coverage

concepts.label: Workspace coverage

concepts.definition: Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T) binds workspace, governed outcome, exact basis, known evaluation inventory, declared frame set and claim time or immutable checkpoint.

grounding.quote:
Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the
workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known
evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable
checkpoint T of the claim.

concepts.label: Exact coverage tuple

concepts.definition: Known material evaluations derived by the coverage evaluator from every material available source, with provenance and materiality recorded.

grounding.quote:
The coverage evaluator derives the known evaluation inventory from every
material available source

concepts.label: Evaluation inventory

concepts.definition: Cross-cutting inventory lenses, typically outcome/capability, identity/authority, lifecycle/temporal behaviour, topology/interaction seams, transport/representation, evidence/proof, change/failure/recovery/rollback, historical regression and actor capability/context fit. They become frames only through separate instantiation as bounded evaluation families.

grounding.quote:
These are lenses (FOUNDATIONS §2): they become frames only when separately
instantiated as bounded evaluation families

concepts.label: Coverage dimensions

concepts.definition: An audit ledger with at least, per evaluation: exact question/predicate; provenance establishing materiality; exact subject and basis; capable selected frames; required competence/context envelope; semantic owner; existing operation grant for construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation when performed, otherwise none; disposition owner; required evidence and provenance; material frame/seam dependencies; coverage status; and uncertainty, exclusion or re-entry residual.

grounding.quote: | operation authority | the existing owner grant for construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation where the evaluation performs one; otherwise none |

concepts.label: Coverage ledger

concepts.definition: Discovery and revision is the source's topic for diagnosing frame problems and proposing changes to declarations, activations, actor assignments and frame sets.

grounding.quote: ## 10. Discovery and revision

concepts.label: Frame discovery and diagnosis

concepts.definition: Revision of frame declarations or the project inventory, with materiality determined by changes to declarations under FOUNDATIONS §2. Revision coordinates and continued validity of already closed results are separate questions.

grounding.quote:
Whether a revision needs a new frame revision coordinate turns on the
frame's declarations; whether a result already closed stays valid is a
separate question.

concepts.label: Frame revision

concepts.definition: The minimum packet for one activated frame or declared active frame configuration: frame identity/revision; evaluation/result algebra; exact subject/basis; material relations/invariants; semantic, evaluation, material operation and decision authorities; admissible evidence/tools; capability/context envelope; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; declared dependencies/conjunction outputs; invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.

grounding.quote:
An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
workspace from ambient context

concepts.label: Activation packet

concepts.definition: Carrier-neutral binding template for one declared frame and evaluation. It contains stable activation identity; declaration identity/revision; exact evaluation/closed algebra; exact subject or candidate identity; workspace, authority, dependency, configuration and time basis; material relations/invariants; exact source/semantic references; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; actor/envelope; semantic/evaluation authority; material operation authority, subject and territory; decision/acceptance/publication authority; admissible evidence/acquisition route; used dependency, overlap, input, conjunction or translation relations; result consumer/return relation; and invalidation, stop, residual, re-entry and reconfiguration conditions.

grounding.quote:
The following carrier-neutral content is sufficient to bind one declared
frame for one evaluation. It may be written in Markdown, structured data, a
prompt or another consumer-selected carrier without changing the relation

concepts.label: Minimal activation binding template

concepts.definition: Three carrier-neutral shapes stated to be the least content declaring a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result, sufficient in Markdown or another consumer-selected carrier. These are document roles, not instantiated evaluations or results.

grounding.quote:
The three carrier-neutral shapes below are the least content that declares
a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result. Each is sufficient as
written in Markdown or any other consumer-selected carrier

concepts.label: Minimal declaration shapes

concepts.definition: Frame declaration template: stable local identity; evaluation questions/predicates/closed algebra; workspace boundary, exact identity and version/time/topology coordinates; material entities/variables/relations/states/interactions; coordinate distinctions and equality; governing invariants; frame-set, semantic, evaluation, material operation and decision authorities; admissible evidence/provenance/exclusions; competence, context, access, tools, evaluation/assurance independence and configuration; irrelevant material/prohibited assumptions/out-of-frame conditions; optional actually used inputs, outputs, overlaps, conjunctions or translations; invalidation/recharting changes; and qualification cases, counterexamples and known residuals.

grounding.quote:
## Optional Frame Relations
<inputs, outputs, overlaps, conjunctions, or translations actually used>

## Invalidation And Recharting
<changes that stale this frame or its results>

## Qualification
<representative cases, counterexamples, and known residuals>

concepts.label: Minimal frame declaration template

concepts.definition: Frame-set declaration template: stable local identity; workspace, outcome, basis and time; human declaration/acceptance authority; known material evaluations/provenance; selected frame identities/revisions/envelopes; evaluation-to-capable-frame coverage rationale; intentional separately activated checks, assurance independence or alternative capability fit; only required conjunction/translation relations; uncovered, unknown, conditional or excluded residual evaluations; and history, topology, capability, evidence or outcome revision triggers.

grounding.quote:
## Residual Uncertainty
<uncovered, unknown, conditional, or excluded evaluations>

## Revision Triggers
<history, topology, capability, evidence, or outcome changes>

concepts.label: Minimal frame-set declaration template

concepts.definition: Evaluation-result template: frame identity/revision; activation identity; evaluation; subject/basis; actor/envelope; semantic, evaluation, material operation and decision authorities; admissible evidence; result; inference relation; residual uncertainty; out_of_frame residual naming missing relation or capability, owner and reconfiguration pressure; invalidation conditions; and consuming decision/conjunction. The out_of_frame residual is none for every other result.

grounding.quote:
The out_of_frame residual field is new in this corpus; it carries what
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) requires an out_of_frame
result to name, and reads `none` for any other result

concepts.label: Minimal evaluation-result template

concepts.definition: A provenance register of predecessor rc.2 REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md anchors received by this member, with loci local unless another member is named. It reports conservation for the listed substantive rows, with exceptions for claimless headings and a nonnormative tier-2 product-chain drift example. Reported changes include distinct communication structure, method/coverage mappings to core values, generalized semantic contraction, diagnostic family-inclusion tightening, default reopening after revision, and the out_of_frame residual field. Ownership remains with the named sections; the family table separates consequences from added choices without deciding them.

grounding.quote:
RF rows received by this member. Rows that land in FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION
or EVALUATION are listed in those members. Anchors are into rc.2
REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless it names
another member.

concepts.label: Source disposition register

concepts.definition: Tier-2 RELEASE owns publication, including release identities, project-qualified refs/subtrees, historical ref conservation, candidate construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification, monotonic version-line advancement, selectors, naming, release-scoped assets, Product subject, coordinated cohorts, acceptance, external qualification dependencies and successor conservation STDO-UP-015. It consumes rather than redefines lineage/release objects, core results/conjunction, effect results, identity, evaluation/acceptance, calculus layer/release separation and identity records, lineage/version boundaries, and installed basis/adoption/toolchain management. Git, tags, branches, stdo:// forms and Specification Stack Product names are Product-specific realization terms.

grounding.quote:
Tier 2. Owns release publication: the release-publication bounded
context, release identities, project-qualified refs and the project
subtree, historical ref conservation, the three phases with candidate
construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification and
monotonic version-line advancement, the selector and its relation to
consumer adoption, naming, release-scoped assets and the Product subject,
coordinated release-matched asset cohorts, acceptance, external
qualification dependencies and successor baseline conservation
(STDO-UP-015) with its disposition values.

concepts.label: Release publication bounded context

concepts.definition: A published point-in-time release cut, bounded, evaluated, named, published and made discoverable by release process. Its product-local name is always v<version>-rc.<n>. It remains distinct from live project specification and from equal local names belonging to other projects.

grounding.quote:
Equal product-local cut
names do not collapse releases owned by different projects

concepts.label: Project-owned immutable RC cut

concepts.definition: The mutable product-local selector v<version>, pointing to the published immutable RC with the greatest positive ordinal for that project and version line. It provides discovery rather than immutable identity.

grounding.quote:
The selector
points to the latest published immutable RC cut on that line, where latest
means the greatest positive RC ordinal published for that project and
version line.

concepts.label: Version-line selector

grounding.quote: this member's law stops at engagement: it defines no application profile, role mapping, product-owned frame-basis binding, domain product, runtime, workflow or assurance implementation.

constraints.statement: The member's identity is urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation and its law stops at engagement. Specializations retain their profile/product authority and neither enter nor amend this context through proximity or matching names. Concepts owned elsewhere retain their owner and meaning through reference-only import, granting no semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority. A local refinement names its owner and maps to the core. The table owns no cited rule; consumer sections decide nothing beyond their owning sections. Core claims add no independent rule, violations restate their cited rules, and source dispositions decide nothing.
constraints.uncertainty: The full import declarations and foundational standing rules are outside the supplied excerpt.

conditions: A frame is claimed to be bound.

grounding.quote: A frame is bound only when every material coordinate resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition, and representation cannot create, widen or replace that binding

constraints.statement: Every material coordinate must resolve to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition. A prompt, packet or program is a projection of an activated frame, and representation cannot create, widen or replace its binding.

conditions: The actor envelope declares context capacity.

grounding.quote: Where the envelope declares a context capacity, the selected context's size is measured before the actor reads it, over a stated boundary, and recorded with the capacity and the comparison; context outside the boundary is recorded as not measured.

constraints.statement: Before reading, measure the selected context across a stated boundary and record its size, capacity and comparison; record context beyond the boundary as not measured. Capacity and bytes/tokens belong to the actor envelope; measured boundary and time, spend and other limits belong to the selected execution binding. The measurement applies only there, shows fit only, and creates neither a budget nor a universal gate.

conditions: Constructing the context for an intake.

grounding.quote: The context starts as the material closure of the intake's seed set (the subject, outcome and affected relations it names) under that relation family, and a closure that is not finite and unique on the exact basis stops the step and is not guessed

constraints.statement: Start from the material closure of the intake's subject, outcome and affected-relation seeds under the material relation family. If closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis, stop without guessing, with closure_unresolved attributed to ACTIVATION §3. Project closure into selected context with a recorded boundary and excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. AC-010 owns closure and AC-011 projection.
constraints.uncertainty: The cited closure and projection laws are not supplied.

conditions: Acquiring declared inputs or activating a reusable declaration.

grounding.quote: declared inputs are acquired by exact identity, and only from the exact selected basis: a declared input absent from the actor's view is neither licence to read elsewhere nor evidence that it is absent

constraints.statement: Acquire inputs by exact identity only from the selected exact basis. Absence from view neither permits another basis nor proves absence; candidate sources, moving selectors and other bases cannot substitute. If a derived surface is stale, missing or insufficient for the named question, acquire the deciding owner sections directly. Acquisition is read-only and grants no role, operation or decision; return a missing binding and its outcome before dependent action. Activation binds the exact subject/basis and loads declared material relations/evidence, never an undifferentiated workspace dump. A reusable declaration proves no particular activation correct. With no lawful available frame/actor pairing, return out_of_frame or the refusal whose cause holds; implied context cannot continue the work. Frame selection belongs to actor or assigning authority as configuration allocates.

conditions: Using a derived surface, projected frame or prompt.
exceptions: Historical workaround prose may be carried when a current surface still needs its constraint.

grounding.quote: For a question another member owns, or one that joins the law of several owners, the step returns `out_of_frame` naming the owning members
a prompt is a rendered contract over typed authority, not source law.

constraints.statement: A derived surface owns no determination and can decide standalone only questions owned by its source members. Questions of another owner or multiple owners return out_of_frame naming them and are decided from those owners or a surface declaring every owner among its sources. A prompt projects current authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations, fallback conditions and acquired material; it has no source authority. Construction starts at the highest live authority surface needed and identifies unresolved upstream authority gaps before reading fallback context.

grounding.quote: frame disjointness (structural), evaluation independence (procedural) and assurance independence (claim-relative) are three relations

constraints.statement: Structural disjointness, procedural evaluation independence and claim-relative assurance independence are distinct. Disjointness does not imply independent evaluation; separate activation does not imply disjointness; unqualified 'independent' establishes none. The governing assurance law determines additional conditions for independent assurance.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §3's assurance-independence conditions are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
9. Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful pressure for
   reconfiguration; they are neither failed evaluations nor implied
   acceptance (P5).
10. Historical failures, resets and invisible violations are evidence for
    improving a frame declaration, an activation, an actor assignment or a
    frame set (P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: No finite actor is presumed to hold the whole material workspace. Useful frames are finite and sufficient for declared evaluation families, whose evaluations determine attention. Human authority may declare practical sets without unique mechanical partitioning; frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate or succeed, with hierarchy optional and internal-coordinate composition unnecessary merely because several frames are used. Coverage is relative to declared workspace, outcome, inventory, basis and time. Breadth, usefulness, actor and technology confer no semantic, operation or decision authority. Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful reconfiguration pressure, neither failed evaluations nor acceptance. Historical failures, resets and invisible violations inform frame, activation, assignment or set improvement.

grounding.quote:
Every frame, declared or activated, obeys the following. The objects named
are defined in FOUNDATIONS §2.

constraints.statement: The following frame laws apply to every declared or activated frame; the named objects are attributed to FOUNDATIONS §2.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

constraints.statement: Every frame must declare its supported evaluation family. Without that declaration there is no testable sufficiency boundary; calling a module, file, service, role, persona, prompt or lens a frame supplies no evaluation relation.

conditions: The frame is activated.

grounding.quote:
An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the
selected actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that needs
undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or an effectively global
workspace context is not reconstructable for that actor

constraints.statement: The attention surface must be finite and fit the selected declared envelope. Requiring undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or effectively global workspace context makes the frame unreconstructable for that actor. ACTIVATION §2 owns context-size measurement and its applicability; fitting size does not establish adequate actual attention.

conditions: A known relation's lawful change can alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency, operation authority or decision authority.
exceptions: No proof of the absence of undiscovered material relations is required.

grounding.quote:
Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
the validity of the basis, the sufficiency of evidence, operation authority
or decision authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared
authoritative input. Omitting a material relation makes the frame
insufficient.

constraints.statement: Every such relation must appear in the frame or enter through a declared authoritative input. Omitting a material relation makes the frame insufficient.

conditions: Relations cannot affect the declared evaluation.
exceptions: They are needed to establish that irrelevance.

grounding.quote:
Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation stay outside active
attention unless they are needed to establish that irrelevance. A frame
does not expand because adjacent workspace material exists

constraints.statement: Keep irrelevant relations outside active attention. Adjacency or the existence of corpus material is no reason to expand the frame or read/load it.

grounding.quote:
Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence
scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns
`invalid_basis` or requires reactivation. Apparent equality never
substitutes for declared coordinate equality

constraints.statement: Every result binds exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope. Stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis yields invalid_basis or requires reactivation. Equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions cannot replace declared coordinate equality; each frame declares its coordinate/equality law.

grounding.quote:
A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
transfer or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation or decision
authority from anything that creates none.

constraints.statement: A frame only carries and applies admitted authority; actor identity, capability, evidence shape, implementation reachability and selection cannot mint, widen, transfer or reconstruct authority. Declaration, selection, activation, execution or naming a role grants none. Read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; effectful evaluation inherits the exact grant from its existing owner. Lawful coincident roles do not collapse authority kinds by default.

grounding.quote:
a frame declaration keeps these roles distinguishable even when
one actor lawfully performs several of them, and where the evaluation
performs a material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the
exact grant as a further role the declaration keeps apart
The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra and records every assumption whose failure could change the result

constraints.statement: Keep semantic law, evidence, evaluator application and disposing decision authority distinguishable, including when one actor lawfully performs several roles. For a material operation keep the existing owner's exact grant as an additional distinct role. Apply declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra and record every assumption whose failure could change the result.

conditions: Frames share material or an evaluation uses cross-frame equality or translation.

grounding.quote:
Shared
material establishes neither identical meaning nor identical basis,
authority or result. Every cross-frame equality or translation an
evaluation uses is declared where it is used

constraints.statement: Sharing entities, variables, evidence or coordinates establishes no identity of meaning, basis, authority or result. Declare every equality or translation where the evaluation uses it.

grounding.quote:
Functional
decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration,
subject topology and evaluation dependency are distinct relation
structures; a consumer may align them where the governed subject warrants
it and may not silently treat them as one hierarchy

constraints.statement: Parent/child relations apply only when explicitly declared. Functional decomposition, communication, authority precedence, configuration, subject topology and evaluation dependency remain distinct. Communication means information exchange between frames or activated actors; by itself it grants no authority and establishes neither decomposition nor evaluation dependency. Configuration assigns exchanges as well as responsibilities; reading an exchange as a grant/dependency would move authority or change results without a declaration.

conditions: The governing evaluation combines internal variables, transports evidence/values across frames, or treats operations as one material execution relation.

grounding.quote:
Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds.
Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines
their internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or
treats their operations as one material execution relation.

constraints.statement: Composition law is required in these cases, not merely from using multiple frames. Independently activated evaluations may instead supply closed results to one declared conjunction or decision rule.

conditions: A material topology mutation is detected or the frame is materially revised.

grounding.quote:
An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating
its coordinates or its materiality judgment. A detected material topology
mutation causes reevaluation, frame revision or recharting before the
previous result is reused. Material revision of the frame itself
invalidates for reuse every result bound to the prior revision coordinate

constraints.statement: Declare topology changes that can invalidate coordinates or materiality judgments. Detected material mutations require reevaluation, revision or recharting before reuse. Material frame revision invalidates every prior-revision-bound result for reuse, subject to the explicit re-check routes in Revision actions.

grounding.quote:
that nothing is
coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result

constraints.statement: Every performed evaluation returns exactly one closed result in its declared core algebra or mapped refinement. No coercion to success is allowed. Refinement adds no core value, raises no result's standing and keeps indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit. A nonperformed evaluation has no evaluation result.
constraints.uncertainty: Full core meanings and algebra rules belong to unsupplied FOUNDATIONS §4.

conditions: A fresh competent actor is inside the declared envelope.

grounding.quote:
A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can
reconstruct the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, the exact
subject, the basis and the admissible inputs, without undocumented
conversational or historical context

constraints.statement: The actor must be able to reconstruct the activated evaluation from its declaration, exact subject, basis and admissible inputs without undocumented conversational or historical context.

conditions: The material manifold exceeds the selected actor's envelope.

grounding.quote:
Choosing among them is human authority's, exercised directly or
in advance through the grant; ACTIVATION §2 says which of them a step
selects itself and which re-enter the grant's owner. The actor may not
silently omit material relations to fit its context

constraints.statement: Adequacy includes actor usability. ACTIVATION §2 owns remedies including another actor, refined frame/outer contract or steps, sequenced activations, lawful compression or out_of_frame. Human authority chooses directly or in advance through its grant; refinement, sequencing and compression may be selected within the grant, whereas another actor or larger envelope re-enters the grant/envelope owner as prescribed there. No silent material omission or envelope growth is allowed. Capability cannot waive invariants or widen authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete remedy-selection conditions are in unsupplied ACTIVATION §2.

grounding.quote:
Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved
relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability
stay explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of
universal completeness

constraints.statement: Coverage and evaluation results must explicitly retain unresolved relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability. No recorded counterexample is not evidence of universal completeness.

conditions: Compressing accumulated practice or merging frames.

grounding.quote:
Intentional overlap is retained where it supplies
independently activated evaluation, different capability fit, different
evidence altitude or useful fault detection. Frames are merged only when
the merged frame preserves evaluation meaning, authority, capability fit
and proportional reasoning cost
the compressing step records the compression and its preservation argument

constraints.statement: Compression must preserve required material distinctions and failure detections while fitting the envelope; a unique smallest frame is unnecessary. Retain overlap that supplies independently activated evaluation, different capability fit/evidence altitude or useful fault detection. Merge only while preserving evaluation meaning, authority, capability fit and proportional reasoning cost. Record compression and its preservation argument; independent assessment of that claim is determined by the promotion it serves.

grounding.quote:
Frame-set contraction asks a different
question: whether two frame declarations support the same evaluation
relation without material difference in evidence, authority, capability
fit, evaluation or assurance independence, or failure detection.

constraints.statement: A frame is activated/evaluated as one bounded engagement atom, not necessarily one irreducible semantic atom. Several semantic atoms may inhabit one frame and one atom may inhabit several frames. An adopting method's semantic-contraction law governs its domain atoms. Frame contraction instead asks whether evaluation relations coincide without material differences in evidence, authority, capability fit, evaluation/assurance independence or failure detection. Overlapping variables alone do not justify contraction to a disjoint minimum.

conditions: Declaring a project frame set.

grounding.quote:
- semantic, evaluation, operation where material, decision and acceptance
  authority;
- known exclusions and residual uncertainty; and
- the conditions for revision.

constraints.statement: Record workspace/outcome, known evaluation inventory, selected frames/envelopes, intentional overlaps/separately activated checks, known dependencies/translations, semantic/evaluation/material operation/decision/acceptance authorities, exclusions/residual uncertainty and revision conditions. Human selection is lawful method structure, but proves neither completeness nor authority over inspected subject relations.

conditions: Selecting S for known material evaluations E(W,G).

grounding.quote:
a
selected frame set S meets the baseline coverage constraint when, for every
evaluation e in E(W, G), there is a frame F in S and an available actor a
inside F's capability envelope K_F such that F with a is capable of e

constraints.statement: Baseline coverage requires, for every e in E(W,G), some F in S and an available actor a within K_F such that F with a can evaluate e. Selection also weighs context/competence, risk/consequence, acquisition/reasoning cost, evidence availability, useful separate overlap, translation/reconciliation cost, historical blind spots and reversibility if inadequate. No optimization algorithm is prescribed. These considerations create no universal ledger, benchmark, budget or measurement gate. Resource controls apply only through an explicitly selected frame and its owning applicability/work scope; ACTIVATION §6 selects cost when cost is the governed question. This weighing is distinct from RF-002 fit measurement. Selection waives no semantic, authority, evidence or independence constraint.

conditions: Interpreting activate outcomes.

grounding.quote: | | `activation_refusal(basis)` | the subject or basis is stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched (RF-005), a topology mismatch included: the subject's topology is not the topology basis the frame declares (RF-011) | `invalid_basis` |

constraints.statement: For the predicate that the frame is activated for this exact evaluation, subject, basis and actor: activated_frame maps to satisfied when the declaration is bound to those inputs; activation_refusal(capability) maps to out_of_frame when a declared required capability is absent from the actor envelope and names the capability and its owner where given; activation_refusal(authority) maps to out_of_frame for required unadmitted semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority and names its owner; activation_refusal(basis) maps to invalid_basis for stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched subject/basis, including topology mismatch. If no usable frame declares a material required relation or capability, activate returns out_of_frame directly. Refusal performs no evaluation, and activation outcomes never answer the evaluation's claim.

conditions: Interpreting conjoin outcomes.

grounding.quote: | | `conflict` | the conjunction reports `falsified` while mandatory results for the same claim disagree, one `satisfied` and another `falsified`; the counterexample survives the join, and the disagreement stays unresolved for the decision authority | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: For the composite predicate under its declared rule: decision(holds) maps to satisfied when the underlying conjunction reports satisfied; decision(fails) maps to falsified when it reports falsified and no mandatory same-claim result is satisfied; conflict maps to falsified when mandatory same-claim results include both satisfied and falsified, preserving the counterexample and unresolved disagreement for decision authority; indeterminate maps to indeterminate. Underlying out_of_frame or invalid_basis is returned directly, including basis mismatch, despite omission from the signature. Declared veto/deferral selects the outcome whose cause holds, or those direct values. Planned assessments lacking closed results and required coverage lacking planned assessment are recorded beside the value and map to no core value. decision(holds) is assessment, not acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: The actual conjunction, veto and deferral laws are delegated to FOUNDATIONS §4.

conditions: Interpreting translate outcomes.

grounding.quote: | | `refusal(authority)` | an authority mismatch the translation does not declare: the value or evidence carries semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority whose relation to the target frame's authority the translation states neither as preserved nor as a refusal condition; the refusal names that authority's owner | `out_of_frame` |

constraints.statement: For entry into the target as declared: translated_value maps to satisfied when meaning is carried into target coordinates; declared_loss maps to satisfied only for loss within declared accepted loss, traveling with the value as a residual. refusal(condition) maps to falsified when a declared refusal condition holds, including excessive loss or failure of declared identity/equality. refusal(authority) maps to out_of_frame for an undeclared authority mismatch whose source-to-target relation is neither preserved nor declared a refusal condition, and names its owner. refusal(basis) maps to invalid_basis for stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched source basis/coordinate. Each refinement outcome carries exactly one core value with its own predicate and meaning; cause-qualified names prevent conflating refusal, conflict or excessive loss with success or a nonperformed evaluation.

conditions: The evaluation requires a relation through which frames act together.

grounding.quote:
Frames act together through four distinct relations, and only where the
evaluation requires one

constraints.statement: Keep independently activated co-evaluation, closed-result conjunction, evidence/coordinate translation and material composition distinct; introduce them only where required by the evaluation.

conditions: Evaluations are independently activated.

grounding.quote:
They may overlap in subject, manifold or
evidence sources; neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's
unclosed working result.

constraints.statement: Neither evaluation may consume or influence the other's unclosed working result, although subject, manifold or evidence sources may overlap.

conditions: A frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another.

grounding.quote:
where the
translation is represented in `a_c` it is recorded in the preservation,
introduced, removed and residual fields of
[AC-013](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-013-transformation).

constraints.statement: Declare source/target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions. ACTIVATION §4 Refinement owns what preservation/loss must show and the licensing law. Where represented in a_c, record preservation, introduced, removed and residual fields under the subject's AC-013. This section adds only frame coordinates, provenance, equality law and refusal fields; it does not independently license translation.
constraints.uncertainty: The cited licensing and transformation laws are not supplied; no transformation is performed here.

conditions: The evaluation requires material composition.

grounding.quote:
The owning application declares the composition, the shared
invariants, the effect or decision order where material, closure, failure,
and the conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.

constraints.statement: The owning application declares composition, shared invariants, material effect/decision order, closure, failure and conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority. A possible future interaction does not impose a general composition law on every frame.

grounding.quote:
No relation is the default universal frame topology. A project declares
only the relations its evaluations and coverage claims need

constraints.statement: No frame relation is a default universal topology. Declare only relations required by project evaluations and coverage claims; governing/subordinate inheritance requires an actual authority or decomposition relation.

conditions: A material member of the exact coverage tuple changes.

grounding.quote:
Changing any material member may invalidate the
coverage result; whether a change does is decided by
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse): it does when it
could change that result, as a material input change or a changed basis

constraints.statement: A material tuple change may invalidate coverage; under ACTIVATION §7 it does when it could change the result as material input or basis change. Material-member change is not automatically equated with every possible invalidation.

exceptions: Each listed source category is included where applicable.

grounding.quote:
The inventory records provenance and
materiality. Artifact presence, file count, operation count, test count or
repository reachability proves no evaluation coverage

constraints.statement: Derive inventory from every material available source, including applicable goals/intent/product definition/requirements/accepted method; accepted design ontology, identities, lifecycles, authorities and algorithms; implementation capabilities and externally observable behaviour; operational/release/security/safety/governance obligations; direct/indirect dependencies and seams; evidence/tests/scenarios/qualification/acceptance claims; historical tickets/check-ins/commentary/post-mortems/incidents/rejected candidates; prolonged loops/resets/repeated repairs/rival paths; actor limitations/invisible violations; and external law/contracts/standards. Record provenance/materiality. Artifact presence, file/operation/test/review/actor counts and repository reachability prove no coverage.

conditions: The coverage tuple is valid for the audit.
exceptions: For stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched tuples, return invalid_basis and assign no status.

grounding.quote:
They answer
whether a row's coverage obligation is met, for the predicate "on the
declared coverage tuple, a capable frame of S covers the evaluation with
no unresolved conflict among the frames, results or authorities that
cover it, or a governing authority the row cites excludes it".

constraints.statement: Statuses answer the row coverage-obligation predicate on the exact tuple and travel with exactly one core value: covered → satisfied when a capable S frame evaluates with no unresolved covering conflict; separately_covered → satisfied when separately activated S frames each evaluate without unresolved conflict; excluded_by_authority → satisfied when the cited governing authority excludes it from the claim; conditionally_covered → indeterminate when a capable frame's condition is unestablished, with residual naming condition and deciding evidence; conflicted → falsified for unresolved conflict among covering frames/results/authorities, retaining that counterexample for decision authority; uncovered → falsified when no capable S frame evaluates and no cited exclusion applies; unknown → indeterminate when admissible evidence cannot decide coverage, including unknown capability/materiality. Values are audit results, never covered-evaluation results. Exclusion meets the obligation without coverage or performance. An uncovered evaluation enters governed-claim conjunction as required coverage lacking planned assessment, not as a falsified component. Conditional, conflicted, unknown and uncovered cannot be read as covered, nor exclusion as failure.

conditions: Covered relations interact in a way capable of changing the governed outcome.

grounding.quote:
Evaluation-row coverage is insufficient when two covered relations interact
in a way capable of changing the governed outcome. Every material
interaction is covered by one frame, a declared conjunction, a translation
or a material composition evaluation

constraints.statement: Row coverage alone is insufficient. Every material interaction must be covered by a frame, declared conjunction, translation or material-composition evaluation.

grounding.quote:
Every material evaluation identifies semantic and decision authority.
Every material operation also identifies its existing construction,
transformation, admission, publication or mutation authority. A frame set
with broad observational reach, an unresolved decision owner or an
effectful path without operation authority is not closed

constraints.statement: Every material evaluation identifies semantic and decision authority; every material operation identifies its existing construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation authority. Unresolved decision ownership or an effectful path without operation authority prevents closure. Broad observational reach cannot establish authority or closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The phrase listing broad observational reach alongside closure defects admits a stronger literal reading; retained separately as a residual.

conditions: Cases are known and material.
exceptions: A historical failure ceases to remain a coverage input when a declared frame detects or excludes its recurrence.

grounding.quote:
Coverage includes known success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery,
reconstruction and competing-path cases where they are material.
Historical failures stay first-class coverage inputs until a declared frame
detects or excludes their recurrence

constraints.statement: Include success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery, reconstruction and competing-path cases. Historical failures persist as first-class coverage inputs until the stated detection/exclusion condition.

conditions: Human authority requires independently activated coverage, potentially for high consequence, weak observability, strong confirmation bias or historical local proof masking.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may require independently activated frame coverage for
evaluations whose failure has high consequence, weak observability, strong
confirmation bias or a history of local proof masking. Such coverage uses a
separately activated evaluation relation and declares any additional
assurance-independence conditions. A persona label alone establishes
neither relation

constraints.statement: Use a separately activated evaluation relation and declare additional assurance-independence conditions. A persona label establishes neither relation. The risk factors permit human authority to require this coverage; they do not impose an automatic universal requirement.

conditions: Claiming operational full coverage for a declared tuple.

grounding.quote:
Operational full coverage is relative to its tuple. It is not a claim that
no undiscovered evaluation exists

constraints.statement: All eight conditions must hold: every known material evaluation has at least one capable covering frame; every material interaction has a declared evaluation/conjunction/translation/composition relation; every evaluation has semantic/decision authority and every material operation inherited operation authority; every mandatory claim has admissible evidence and refusal paths; required separate overlaps and assurance-independence conditions are present; aggregation hides no unresolved frame-result conflict; excluded evaluations cite governing authority; and uncovered/unknown residuals are explicit and compatible with the claim. Coverage is tuple-relative, not absence of undiscovered evaluations.
constraints.uncertainty: The supplied text does not fully resolve how the universal first condition interacts with permitted exclusions and compatible uncovered residuals.

exceptions: A finite formally closed domain may support exhaustive coverage relative to an independently established completeness predicate, without generalization beyond that domain.

grounding.quote:
Without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate,
a finite frame set cannot establish the absence of every undiscovered
material evaluation by inspecting its own declared inventory.

constraints.statement: Inventory self-inspection does not establish absence of undiscovered material evaluations without the stated independent predicate. Formal incompleteness results motivate caution but do not prove this particular workspace/set incomplete. Coverage remains falsifiable and externally challengeable, with an explicit residual boundary and no metaphysical/universal completeness claim. Challenges include outside human knowledge, independent review, history/predecessors, mutation/adversarial/counterexample searches, live use, adjacent-domain comparison and actor, law, dependency or topology changes. The domain owner independently establishes any closed-domain predicate.

conditions: Any listed observation occurs.

grounding.quote:
- two actors use the same frame name but evaluate different material
  relations; or
- a topology mutation leaves prior verdicts apparently current.

constraints.statement: Trigger diagnosis when a competent actor repeatedly misses a known material violation; repair creates/duplicates an authority path; work repeatedly resets after apparent local completion; long loops fail stable closure; proof passes with outcome unbound; failure emerges only after broad integration; reviewers repeatedly expand context without a decidable question; same-named frames evaluate different material relations; or topology change leaves prior verdicts apparently current. These signals are evidence for diagnosis, not repair authority.

conditions: Diagnosing a frame problem.

grounding.quote: Question 1 is answered by family inclusion, not by set membership.

constraints.statement: Ask in order: correct declared frame activated; exact subject/basis; actor within envelope; admissible evidence available; missing material variable/invariant; missing required conjunction/translation; wrong/incomplete family; another frame required. The first question tests whether the actual decided question belongs to the declared family at declared coordinates. Set membership, frame/role labels and similar wording do not establish inclusion or trigger activation; outside-family activation answers no regardless of frame standing. This order prevents every difficulty automatically creating a frame.

conditions: A frame declaration is materially revised.
exceptions: A reopened result leaves the list through a recorded re-check demonstrating independence from the change or reevaluation on the new revision.

grounding.quote:
The revision record lists those
results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check
that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation
on the new revision. A material revision does not select which of the
results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep
a result closed.

constraints.statement: Every material revision changes frame identity/revision coordinates, creates a new revision coordinate for a materially changed frame, and states affected prior activations, results and coverage claims. Every closed result bound to the previous revision becomes mismatched and invalid for reuse; record all as reopened. Selective reopening or silence cannot preserve closure.

conditions: Considering result reuse, including when no declaration changed.
exceptions: A harmless explanatory clarification changing no material input and constituting no revising observation invalidates no result by itself; exact applicability checking still applies.

grounding.quote:
an unchanged declaration is no ground for
keeping a result closed.

constraints.statement: No declaration change needs no new coordinate, but decides nothing about result validity. ACTIVATION §7 reuse with FOUNDATIONS materiality may reopen results without revision; record these in work state under ACTIVATION §5. Discovering outside-family activation or acquiring admissible evidence material to a closed result reopens that result and every consuming coverage row/claim, while preserving demonstrably independent survivors. Every reuse still requires the consumer's exact applicability check.
constraints.uncertainty: Complete reuse and materiality definitions remain external.

grounding.quote:
Hidden
internal reasoning is no substitute for required evidence, provenance or
authority

constraints.statement: Supply one activated frame or declared configuration without demanding ambient reconstruction of the whole workspace. Return through the declared result relation; hidden reasoning substitutes for no required evidence, provenance or authority. Optimize size for reliable evaluation rather than maximum loading. Broader frames for more capable actors and lawful refinement sequences for less capable actors must preserve the same material invariants and authority relations.

grounding.quote:
Every field resolves through stable identities and source references.
Paths, line numbers, member counts, summaries and matching labels may aid
navigation or diagnostics; they do not substitute for the declared identity
and basis

constraints.statement: Every binding field resolves through stable identities and source references. Paths, line numbers, counts, summaries and matching labels may aid navigation or diagnosis but cannot substitute for declared identity and basis.

conditions: The practice supports a frame or coverage claim.

grounding.quote:
Each of the following is a violation of this member where it supports a
frame or coverage claim

constraints.statement: Violations are: presumed omniscient frame; calling a carrier/role/lens a frame without evaluation relation; silently merging decomposition, authority hierarchy and topology into one tree; requiring every active frame to compose with every other; composition machinery without material cross-frame evaluation; treating selection/visibility as semantic authority; flattening evidence across bases/coordinates into one executed/observed relation; returning satisfied instead of lawful indeterminate/out_of_frame/invalid_basis; inferring coverage from artifact/file/operation/test/review/actor counts; silent envelope growth; stale activation reuse after topology mutation without recharting; adding a frame for every failure before excluding activation/basis/evidence/capability/evaluation defects; contracting overlap with independent failure detection or material capability differences; and presenting generic runtime/registry/controller/universal carrier as required.

conditions: A project claims to operate under this member.

grounding.quote:
8. no executable frame machinery, global context, universal completeness
   or domain authority is inferred from adopting this member

constraints.statement: Human authority has declared workspace, outcome, inventory and set; every active frame is finite, evaluation-bound, basis-bound, authority-safe and usable within its envelope; results preserve semantic/evidence/inference/decision distinctions; cross-frame conjunction/translation/composition exists only for material evaluation needs; every known material evaluation/interaction maps to a capable frame or explicit residual; operational coverage is exact-tuple-relative; topology, capability, evidence and history can trigger revision/recharting; and adoption implies no executable machinery, global context, universal completeness or domain authority.

grounding.quote:
it decides nothing
and names the rule that states each consequence.

constraints.statement: The predecessor reference-frame-laws, workspace-coverage and discovery/revision headings are recorded as not applicable because they contain no claim text; children are disposed separately. The worked product-chain-drift binding is recorded as not applicable because it is a nonnormative example adding no determination to the conserved binding, with tier-2 subject matter whose successor worked binding belongs to qualification against its owner. Other listed received rows are reported conserved with their stated refinements/ownership transfers. F1 is reported new with no predecessor row, but its table decides nothing and must not present added choices as derived.
constraints.uncertainty: These are source-authored conservation/disposition claims, not independently verified equivalence judgments.

grounding.quote:
A route written `rc.2 #anchor` is
into `stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/RELEASE_METHOD.md` and is
provenance only; every predecessor row received here is restated in this
text, and nothing here depends on that cut to be applied.

constraints.statement: RELEASE consumes external owners' meanings without redefining them. Every clause names its requiring P0–P6 principle. rc.2 anchor routes are provenance into the predecessor RELEASE_METHOD.md, not an application dependency on that cut. Its bounded context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication under the selected complete STDO basis; it owns release qualification/publication/selection identities and transitions, not Product meaning or consumer adoption, whose consumer side belongs to PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4.
constraints.uncertainty: The announced later release clauses and external owners are not included.

grounding.quote:
Release handling is downstream of intake triage. A bug, feature,
regression or release blocker first receives its change class, lawful
re-entry point, affected scope, downstream proof obligations and
version-line disposition

constraints.statement: Live specification states current constitutional project truth; release process handles a published point-in-time cut. Product-local cut names are always v<version>-rc.<n>; shared release sources use this as a project-qualified Git-ref suffix, preserving separate project identities despite equal local names. v<version> is mutable discovery and insufficient as exact constitutional, dependency, evidence or replay basis. Before release handling, every bug, feature, regression or blocker receives change class, lawful re-entry, scope, downstream proof duties and version-line disposition under SPEC_METHOD §4. An RC window authorizes no untriaged mutation.
constraints.uncertainty: Project-qualified ref details reside in unsupplied RELEASE §2.

conditions: A release operation is refused/stops/fails closed, or a release-state/cohort/verification check fails.

grounding.quote:
Where it says
that an operation is refused, stops or fails closed, the operation does
not complete; its intended effect, with any part of it that began, is
reported under [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects), never as
`completed`.

constraints.statement: RELEASE defines no independent result values. A refused, stopped or fail-closed operation does not complete; report the intended effect and any partial beginning under ACTIVATION §3 Effects, never completed. Invalid release state, incomplete cohort or failed verification supplies a counterexample to that check's predicate and returns under FOUNDATIONS §4. Section 9 separately states its disposition values. Refused publication or failed verification is never interpreted as a published or qualified cut.
